Good morning. I'm presenting Reimagining the Personal Music Experience — a privacy-first personalisation layer for Spotify, YouTube Music and Apple Music, backed by survey data and a working Python backend.

Music streaming is routine for our respondents, but personalisation is uneven. Only 39% say their app understands their taste very well. This project asks whether a lightweight utility can improve discovery and rediscovery without needing account APIs.

Objectives: control over recommendation familiarity, easy rediscovery of saved music, and statistical proof. Outcomes are a Chrome extension, a responsive Flask dashboard with SQLite, and an analysis pipeline that reruns on updated data.

We used convenience sampling of students. The questionnaire mixes multiple choice, ordinal ratings, numeric age and three open-ended questions. 18 responses — below the target of 30, which we state openly. The sample is 78% Spotify.
Users say remove ads and better recommendations. They do save songs — 78% — but 44% struggle to find old saves. Ranked pain points: ads 50%, out of scope; recommendations and retrieval both 44%.

One-sample t-tests against neutral show responses above neutral for vibe ease and taste understanding. Saved retrieval was not significant. Correlations were weak. So we do not overclaim: the baseline is good-but-not-great and the opportunity is refinement.

Our composite persona is Aarav, a 19-year-old daily Spotify user. POV: a listener who saves but cannot rediscover and feels recommendations only somewhat match their taste. HMW: how might we give that control without a paid subscription? MoSCoW puts Discover, My Music and the backend in Must.
We generated ten ideas, from a discovery slider and vibe tags to an AI chatbot and an ad blocker, mapped them across five branches, then scored each on desirability, feasibility and viability.

Weighted scoring put the discovery slider, vibe tags and save-plus-library at 5.00. The AI chatbot scored 2.45 and ad blocker 2.80 — rejected on feasibility. Before testing we fixed three hypotheses at alpha 0.05.

The prototype has two parts: a Chrome extension with per-platform adapters, and a responsive Flask dashboard with SQLite. Everything stays local — no login, no external API. Let me demonstrate: Discover, save a song, My Music, Vibe, and the study page.

Testing uses the same participants on both methods. The study page times three tasks and counts clicks and errors, then computes SUS. For time, Wilcoxon if non-normal otherwise paired t-test; for SUS a one-sample t-test against 68. Insert actual results here once runs are complete.

Iteration one: we split track detection into per-platform adapters after the single-file version broke on YouTube Music. Iteration two: a dashboard gave saved songs a view. Iteration three: usage logging and a consent toggle made testing measurable.

Benefits: no account required, data never leaves the browser, three platforms. Limitations: n=18 not 30, 78% Spotify and zero Apple Music, ads out of scope, demo recommendation data, and single-contributor scope. We disclose all of these.

We learned that a small focused utility can address a real measured gap — saved-song retrieval and taste control — without complex infrastructure. Future work: a real recommendation model, the Understand section, and a larger stratified sample.
